edges.description: Accumulated proinflammatory LPS lipids promote microglial activation and neurobehavioral abnormalities in the ABHD12-deficient brain model.

Human ABHD12-related PHARC includes macular and retinal degeneration, although the tissue-specific lipid intermediates linking dysregulated lysophosphatidylserine metabolism to retinal degeneration remain unresolved.
Human ABHD12-related PHARC includes early-onset and congenital lens opacification, although the exact lipid-mediated ocular intermediates are not resolved by cached abstract evidence.
Microglial activation and neuroinflammatory lipid signaling contribute to auditory and motor abnormalities resembling PHARC.
Peripheral nerve degeneration contributes to sensory and motor deficits.
Cerebellar dysfunction causes progressive gait and coordination impairment.
Auditory-system involvement contributes to the hearing-loss component of PHARC syndrome.
Central corticospinal involvement produces pyramidal tract signs in a substantial subset of PHARC patients.
Peripheral nerve degeneration is expressed clinically as polyneuropathy.
Cerebellar degeneration is expressed clinically as ataxia.
Progressive cerebellar neurodegeneration manifests structurally as cerebellar atrophy on neuroimaging.
Auditory pathway degeneration is expressed clinically as sensorineural hearing impairment.
Retinal degeneration is expressed clinically as rod-cone dystrophy/retinitis pigmentosa.
Progressive outer retinal and retinal pigment epithelium degeneration produces central macular atrophy.
Retinal degeneration produces intraretinal bone-spicule hyperpigmentation and pigmentary alterations.
Lens opacification manifests clinically as congenital or early-onset cataract.
Increased LPS lipids report the lipid-metabolism abnormality downstream of ABHD12 loss in the PHARC model.
